task: Consolidate database work within one accepted race while keeping the checker and atomic scoring/rewards

requirements.RSQL01: Reduce repeated claim/finalization SQL without batching separate races or adding eventual consistency.
requirements.RSQL02: Bound shared acceptance reads and reward milestone reads independently of total account/board population.
requirements.RSQL03: Measure original/current real-checker worker jobs on local isolated PostgreSQL schemas.
requirements.RSQL04: Exercise same-player parallel workers, retries, late rollback, account restriction, reward caps and competition rules.
requirements.R01: Keep checker/build/content/timing policy, Player-to-Run locks, leases and durable idempotent receipts.
requirements.Q01: Record commands, actual outcomes, original failures, source fingerprints, review patch and acceptance limits.

changes.claim: Fetch Run/Board/TrackVersion/Player in the existing single-row SKIP LOCKED claim. Reuse the pinned-filter expression. Claim still locks only Run; account eligibility is reread under the finalization Player lock.
changes.acceptance: One transaction-local indexed join loads Board/TrackVersion/Track, optional competition bindings, receipt/wallet and prior race/lap tick scalars. Each join is one-to-one; no population/history result set is loaded. Missing bindings/receipt are explicitly retained. References live only through this race transaction, not in a shared cache.
changes.previous_bests: Capture scalar PB times before marking Run verified, retaining pre-trigger lap minima and precise PB reward/competition semantics.
changes.milestones: Read at most six exact primary-key scopes in one query. Reuse mutations locally and allow normal ORM flushes to group pending changes. Once a permanent track marker exists, omit the historical-run existence query; historical runs without markers retain the original first-track eligibility check.
changes.wallet: Reuse the already locked Player and wallet fact. The original finalization SELECT emits PostgreSQL FOR NO KEY UPDATE, which serializes ordinary Player-locking wallet writers. Standalone economy/purchase/import callers retain locked_wallet and its original lock/read path.
changes.ledger: Insert the original opening and earned ledger identities in one two-row ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING statement. Preserve existing opening balances/revisions and historical entries. Wallet, milestones, CoinReward, PBs, achievements, competition outcomes and captured news still share one commit. The transaction-local receipt is updated so a repeated writer call cannot mint twice.
changes.checker: No edits to trajectory_verifier.py, verifier.py or json_data.py. No validation, timing, geometry, resource or acceptance check is removed. No native simulation was added to warm acceptance.

measurement.design: Two alternating original/current process pairs, each using a freshly migrated disposable PostgreSQL schema and 40 unprofiled warm samples after two warm-up races: 80 samples per variant. PostgreSQL tests finished before these measurements. No injected round-trip delay.
measurement.fixture: 2130 trajectory samples, pinned native-generated geometry from Godot4.7.2, real Python checker, exact12757 ticks and laps2634/2532/2531/2530/2530. Every timed job asserts its verified result, reward receipt and exact wallet balance. Native invocation is forbidden during measured acceptance.
measurement.scope: Complete process_one claim through commit, warm local object files and SQLite-free PostgreSQL; steady tied repeat races on the player-owned published track. First/new PB/competition paths are correctness-tested separately, not timed here.
measurement.limits: Excludes upload, HTTP, cloud object/network latency, optional ghost artifacts, production queue/poll waiting, cold content churn and sustained concurrent capacity. SQL counts are driver-issued statements; implicit transactions and trigger-internal work are not counted. The shared Windows/WSL host is variable. This is not a million-DAU capacity or a halved database-CPU claim.
measurement.initial_observations: Before final ledger batching, baseline-pg.json and consolidated-pg.json showed47 to27 statements. Final claims use the alternating *-pg-pair files only.
